newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia 1996 gold output at record - analyst.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia 1996 gold output at record - analyst.

text.p: Australian gold output reached a record 292 tonnes in 1996, up 15 percent from 1995, mining consultant Surbiton Associates Pty Ltd said on Monday.
Gold production for 1997 is expected to increase further despite declining gold prices as new mines and upgrades to existing ones commence, Surbiton said in a report.
At least four new mines are scheduled to start production in the first quarter alone, the report noted.
Average cash operating costs among gold miners representing 76 percent of the industry increased A$5 to A$374 an ounce in the December quarter from the previous three months, it said.
"This indicates a reasonably healthy margin for most producers, even at current gold prices," the report said.
Gold in Australian dollars terms is trading at or near five-year lows of around A$446 an ounce.
December quarter gold production rose 15 percent to 76 tonnes compared with a year earlier, Surbiton said.
The value of Australian gold production last year was about A$4.2 billion based on current gold prices, making it the nation's second largest export earner after coal.
Taking into account forward sales, the actual dollar value was probably closer to A$5 billion, the report said.
